title: Linter throws 'invalid array index type' error despite dynamic type of that index, if the function returns null
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in v4.5.stable.official [876b29033] and v4.4.1.stable.official [49a5bc7b6] ### System information Godot v4.5.stable - Linux Mint 22.1 (Xia) on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 (nvidia; 575.64.03) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-7700HQ CPU @ 2.80GHz (8 threads) - 15.51 GiB memory ### Issue description Excuse the lengthy title. GDScript linter throws an 'Invalid index type "null" for a base of type "Array".' error despite not actually knowing the type of index variable used, and the code being safe to use. This only occurs if the return value is set to null, if return is omitted entirely no error is thrown (I assume because in that case the return value is Nil, not Null). See attached image for clarification - gray line numbers suggest it does not know value types, yet the error is present. Usecase: This issue can be bypassed by coding an invalid id as a number, instead of null (a number of built-in functions in godot uses -1 for that purpose). However that limits the ability of utilising negative indexes to count from the end of the array, and using a specific magic number seems like bad practice. This is bypassable by inverting the if statement at line 6 (if a -> if !a) and restructuring the code around that, but that may prove inconvenient in other, larger funcitons and this behaviour does not seem intentional either way. ### Steps to reproduce Create an empty project, create a script and add the following code to it. Linter will throw an error. Comment out `return null` on line eight, the error will disappear. ```gdscript extends Node3D var dict = [] func index_id(a): if a: return randi() return null func dict_lookup(): var id = index_id(bool(randi())) if id != null: return dict[id] ``` ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) N/A
